name: cursor
measures: Scenario 4, the cockpit cursor in five stretches, each a slow path with a slow approach (120 window px/s; the path 50 px/s) and a capture window in both layers around the whole path (56 consecutive submissions, full resolution in both arms over the same tangent window): a-panel = on the up-front panel at the lower edge of the focus image, HUD symbology out of the capture window; b-hud = over the HUD; c-periphery = on the centre panel below the focus image; d-border = slowly to and fro across the focus image's lower border; e-jump = a deliberate jump (the mouse is set in one step) to the sky left of the HUD, then a slow circle. Places are tangents of the view (rig\cursor-calibration.json, measured in a cursor-calib flight). mouse.csv has every mouse step with the capture's clock. cursor_verdict.py: smooth_cursor result=1 / result=6 per second and per stretch, ON against the twin.
cannotJudge: The cursor crossing the focus edge with a moving gaze (needs the gaze scenario without the mouse coupling = a new Quad Views test key). The feel of the cursor. The blob measure only works while the cursor is the brightest mark of the crop: in a lit cockpit read the counters and the cursor-capture pictures first.

verdict.cropsAre: a guess (tangents around the view centre): set from the first capture

sideEffects: the OS mouse cursor is driven for 80 s with DCS in the foreground: do not touch the mouse
with the untracked headset the focus box is centred and the HUD is always inside the focus image; the instrument panel proper is below it (stretch c)

the cursor seen in the calibration flight is the yellow cross (about 48 px in the focus image), over the HUD and the sky and on the panels alike; the white dot (image 149) appears elsewhere: the fixtures say which shape each frame holds
